answer: Operator Liability Escrow. Each identity registers against a legal entity that posts a sable deposit held by the registry, not by the wallet. When correlated identities are detected, the registry slashes the operator's entire escrow and raises their future deposit requirement, while wallets stay untouched. An attacker forging N identities must fund N entity deposits plus a nectar penalty multiplier on every subsequent registration. Repeated abuse triggers a spiral of escalating escrow minimums across all linked entities, making each additional fake identity cost more than the last.
